I am 59 years old. I never went to school, not even one day. My father taught me to farm, and I have been doing it for 40 years. Our family has 12 mu of good flat land in Quzhou. We grow winter wheat and summer corn, switching every season. My two sons work in a factory in Handan and send money home, so I can buy inputs, but I still count every yuan. I do not trust new ideas unless I see them work on my neighbor's field first.

For wheat, I do what I did last year. After the corn comes off in June, I run the rotary tiller over the field to break up the stalks. I plant 30 jin of wheat seed per mu — the kind called Luyuan 502 that my nephew bought last year and had good luck with. It is not the old traditional wheat, it is the improved kind. At sowing in October, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 jin per mu, the red bags from the dealer that everyone in the village uses. I cannot read the numbers on the bag, but I know it is the wheat fertilizer. Then in March, when the wheat starts growing fast and the stems get long, I topdress half a bag of urea — 50 jin per mu. I would rather put a little too much than too little. Last year Old Wang tried to save money on fertilizer and his wheat turned yellow and short. I irrigate three times from my well: once before winter if the ground is dry, once at jointing when the wheat shoots up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray four times total — herbicide once when the weeds are small, insecticide twice because the aphids always come, and fungicide once because my brother-in-law lost half his yield to rust two years ago. I expect about 1000 jin per mu this year if the weather holds, which is 500 kg.

For corn, after we harvest the wheat in early June, I do not till the field anymore. I learned from my cousin that no-tillage works fine for corn and saves diesel money. I plant Denghai 605 hybrid corn, one packet per mu. At planting, I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the row — the dealer gives me the bags for corn. I do not topdress corn because by August the plants are too tall and I am too busy anyway. The soil is still good from the wheat fertilizer. I irrigate twice — once when the corn is knee-high if there has been no rain, and once when the tassels come out. That is the most important time. I spray three times — herbicide once, and insecticide twice for the corn borer. I expect about 1100 jin per mu, which is 550 kg.

I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone puts 100 jin of compound on wheat, I do the same. A bad harvest means disaster — you cannot feed the family or pay for the next year's inputs. Wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost.
